markup.title: Your markup
markup.intro: What your customers pay on top of your cost price. It affects one thing only: the final price. Your cost price is set in your agreement with us — if it changes, final prices follow automatically without you touching this number.
markup.label: Markup in percent
markup.range: Must be between 0 and 500. Below 0 you would be selling at a loss.
markup.example: A typical promo video — 20 seconds, four animated scenes with voiceover:
markup.zero: At 0 % you sell at cost. You earn nothing on productions — which can be deliberate if you make your money elsewhere.
markup.receipt: ✅ Saved. New prices apply from your next production — anything already produced keeps the price it ran at.
markup.why: We state the markup in percent, not kroner, because the cost price can change. The markup then follows along instead of becoming an amount that quietly goes wrong. What you have actually earned is on the

settlement.title: Settlement
settlement.intro: What your customers used in the period, and how much goes to you. Settlement follows usage — credits bought but not yet used don't count.
settlement.none: No usage recorded in this period.
settlement.vat: Figures exclude VAT. Credits bought in advance stay as unused balance until they are actually spent — so revenue here can be lower than what was purchased in the period.
settlement.collectedHint: Card payments we have received on your customers' behalf
settlement.discountFactorHint: Credit packages include a volume discount, so cash received is lower than the spending power granted. Your share is adjusted by the same ratio.
settlement.dueHint: This is what we pay out at the monthly settlement
settlement.noCustomers: No customers with activity this period.

partners.title: Partners
partners.intro: {name}'s direct sub-tiers — the markup they take from their own customers, the licence fee from the partner agreement, and their brand (name, logo and colours on their own domain).
partners.none: No partners under this tier yet.
partners.noneWho: You are seeing this as {slug}. The partner list follows the domain you are signed in on — on the wrong address, you see the wrong tier.
partners.infraSub: The platform's 3 % of voice and face revenue across ALL banks in the tree — rights handling, logging and payout.
partners.infraNone: No asset revenue in the tree this month yet.
partners.ourMarkupHint: Our margin. Sets the cost price {name} is invoiced — and nothing else. 100 % = today's level.
partners.theirMarkupWarn: You are overriding {name}'s own number. They will see the change as their own.
partners.theirMarkupHint: Decides what the end customer pays: cost price × (1 + markup/100). This is the partner's decision — they set it themselves under «Markup».

occasion.inProgressHint: This usually takes a few minutes. You can close the page and come back.
occasion.failedHint: The film was not finished. Try making it again — and tell us if it happens again.
occasion.shareHint: Download the film and send it on Messenger, WhatsApp or e-mail, or post it on Facebook. “Share link” gives you a link straight to the film.
occasion.deleteConfirm: Delete this film? This cannot be undone.
occasion.unfinishedHint: You paid for this film but it was not completed. Press to create the pictures and start the film.
occasion.makeAnotherHint: Just want to change something in the film you have? Use “Edit the posters” under the film — it is free. This button starts from the beginning.
occasion.yourFilmsHint: Want to change something? Press “Edit the posters” — the song, pictures and form are kept, and you go straight to the texts. Text changes cost nothing.

audition.title: Audition
audition.intro: Write the line once, pick who should read it, and see them side by side. Everything but the actor is identical — that is what lets you compare people rather than pictures.
audition.login_title: Sign in to run an audition
audition.login_body: Auditions cost money and pay the actors, so they are charged to an account.
audition.line_placeholder: One line, exactly as it reads in the script.
audition.scene_note: The same scene for everyone. Change it and it changes for the whole round — the point is that only the face varies.
audition.none_ready: Nobody is ready yet. An audition requires the actor to have both a voice and a face model.
audition.price_note: Reads cost {lesning} kr per actor and can be repeated. You order film afterwards, per actor, at {film} kr.
audition.choose_first: Choose a read before you order film.
audition.meta_description: The same scene, the same line, different performers — hear them read your own script before you decide.

twinledger.meta_title: TwinLedger — cleared voices and faces for film and advertising
twinledger.meta_description: The voice and face you want — cleared, logged and paid for. Behind every use is the agreement that permits it, and the performer is paid every time.
twinledger.hero_eyebrow: Cleared voices and faces for film, advertising and games
twinledger.hero_h1_a: The voice and face you want.
twinledger.hero_body: TwinLedger is where a performer’s voice and face are licensed. Every use is logged against the agreement that permits it — and the performer is paid.
twinledger.casting_h2: Hear your own lines, in their voice, before you decide
twinledger.c1_p: Every voice and face in the catalogue belongs to a person who agreed to it, on terms recorded at the moment they agreed.
twinledger.c2_p: Write one line, pick who reads it, and compare them side by side. Same scene, same framing — only the performer changes. They are paid for the audition.
twinledger.c3_h: A licence, not a metered API
twinledger.c3_p: Buy the right you actually need: medium, territory, term — or a one-off buyout bound to the work, for film and scripted television.
twinledger.ledger_h2: One use, one line, written as it happens
twinledger.ledger_body: Nobody reconstructs afterwards how many times a voice or a face was used. It is in the book — and that is why a performer can say yes without having to trust anyone.
twinledger.ledger_note: Illustration. Every line points at the licence that permits it — that is what makes this a clearance record and not a usage meter.
twinledger.line_h2: Clearing and management — with production in-house
twinledger.is_p: Someone other than the person uses their voice or face, and that person is paid for it. Those two things together are what makes a ledger necessary.
twinledger.isnot_p: Our own production unit. With the licence in place we make the film, the spot or the avatar — <cf>CenterForge</cf> is the same house, not a different supplier.
twinledger.line_body: Using your own voice in your own material needs no ledger — that is ordinary production. Partners who only produce content should not inherit the obligations that come with one.
twinledger.door_cast_p: Browse the catalogue, hear them read your own script, and buy the right you actually need.
twinledger.door_talent_h: You have a voice or a face
twinledger.door_talent_p: You decide who may use it. Every use is recorded in a ledger you can see yourself, and you are paid every time.
twinledger.talent_eyebrow: Do you have a voice or a face?
twinledger.t1_p: You choose who may use your voice and face, and for what. Require pre-approval and every use comes to you before it is published.
twinledger.t2_h: The same book as the customer
twinledger.t2_p: Every use is recorded the second it happens — not reconstructed afterwards. You see what it earned, what has been paid, and what is still owed.
twinledger.t3_p: With an archive from a long career, your face can be offered at several ages. A flashback becomes a casting decision — and that is an offer only those with a history can make.
twinledger.agency_h2: Do you bring performers, and look for them?
twinledger.agency_p: Casting agents sit on both sides of the table. You can manage your own rights holders in your own brand, with your prices and your terms — and use the catalogue as a customer when the role needs someone you do not have.

apply.closed_title: {tenant} is not accepting open applications right now
apply.closed_body: You are welcome to get in touch directly if you want to offer your voice.
apply.consent: I consent to my voice samples being assessed for inclusion in the voice bank. If I am accepted, a professional voice clone is created, stored with the platform and never handed out. All use is logged and paid according to agreement, and I may withdraw my voice at any time. My voice is biometric data and is processed in line with data protection rules.
apply.done_body: We will listen to your samples and get in touch at {email}.
apply.intro: Do you have a voice people listen to? Send us a couple of samples — if you join the bank, you earn a royalty every time your voice is used, and you decide who may use it.
apply.f_bio: A little about you and your voice
apply.bio_placeholder: For example experience, accent, what your voice suits
apply.samples_note: MP3, WAV or M4A — max {mb} MB per file. 30–60 seconds of natural speech is perfect.
apply.err_name: Fill in your name and a valid email address.
apply.err_asset: Choose at least one asset: voice or face.
apply.err_sample: Upload at least one voice sample when you offer your voice.
apply.err_consent: You must consent in order to send the application.
apply.err_generic: Something went wrong — please try again.
apply.err_type: “{name}” must be MP3, WAV or M4A.
apply.casting_intro: This is what producers filter on when they are looking for someone. Leave the fields empty and you will not come up in searches — you become invisible, not broadly available.
apply.casting_age_hint: PLAYING AGE, not your age: what age you can play. A wide range gives more hits.
apply.casting_optional: Everything here is optional, and can be changed later.
apply.appearance_consent: I want to state which roles my face can plausibly play
apply.appearance_consent_text: I state myself which roles my face can plausibly play, and consent to this being stored and used for casting. I understand that this counts as a special category of personal data, that it is my own assessment and not a classification of me, and that I can withdraw it at any time — upon which the values are deleted.
apply.appearance_hint: If you do not tick this, nothing is stored in this field.
apply.err_age: Playing age must be numbers, and from cannot be higher than to.
apply.err_height: Height must be between 50 and 260 cm.
apply.meta_description: Do you have a voice people listen to? Become a rights holder at {tenant}: you decide who may use your voice and face, every use is recorded in a ledger you can see, and you are paid every time.

myLedger.signed_out_title: See what your voice has earned
myLedger.signed_out_body: Sign in with the email address you gave us when we made the agreement. You will then see every single time your voice or face has been used, what it earned, and what has been paid out.
myLedger.signed_out_note: No account yet? Create one with the same email as in the agreement — it links up automatically.
myLedger.no_deal_body: The ledger is linked to the email address in your management agreement. Did you sign in with a different address than the one you gave {tenant}? Log out and try that one — or get in touch and we will fix it.
myLedger.split_meter: is payment per use of the voice.
myLedger.licences_h2: Licences — what your voice is cleared for
myLedger.no_statement: No statement yet. Streaming income is reported 2–3 months in arrears.
myLedger.rates_note: A preview is when a customer tests your voice on a text before ordering — each test pays a small amount based on the text length. The rate that applied when the use happened is the one in the book — changes only take effect going forward.
myLedger.uses_h2_voice: Every time your voice has been used
myLedger.uses_h2_face: Every time your face has been used
myLedger.uses_none: Not used yet. Every use appears here the second it happens — not reconstructed afterwards.
myLedger.capped: Showing the last 200. The totals at the top cover everything.
myLedger.footer_note: The amounts are what you receive, before tax. Payout is made by {tenant}. Questions about a line? Get in touch with them.

catalog.intro: Real people you can use in what you make at {tenant}. The price applies per use and comes on top of the production itself. The performer is paid every time, and everything is recorded in a ledger both parties can see.
catalog.err_login: You must be signed in to see the voices.
catalog.picked: {name} is selected for your next video. Go to Overview, open what you want to make a video for, and start a new one — the voice is set when the draft opens.
catalog.empty_body: The bank is empty for now. The standard voices in the tool work as before — they are included and cost nothing extra.
catalog.demo_note: Test profile — cannot be used in a production

approval.intro_face: A customer wants to publish an image with the face of {name}. Review the content below.
approval.intro_voice: A customer wants to publish an audio clip with the voice of {name}. Review the content below.
approval.rejected_note: You rejected this use. The customer cannot use the content.
approval.expired_note: The deadline ({deadline}) has passed — the use is automatically approved under the agreement.
approval.approved_timeout_note: This use was automatically approved (the deadline ran out).
approval.deadline_note: If you do not reply by {deadline}, the use is automatically approved so the customer makes their deadline.
approval.done_approved: Approved — the customer can now use the content. Thank you.
approval.done_rejected: Rejected — the customer cannot use the content.

bank.intro: {who} — rates, use and what is to be paid out. Volume discounts and any shares are calculated at the monthly settlement, not here.
bank.intro_who_tenant: The performers’ voices and faces at {tenant}
bank.err_login: You must be signed in to see this page.
bank.subs_note: Onboarding covered for {n} performers — one month of ElevenLabs Creator each, {sum} in total. A one-off cost, not running: the split survives the performer downgrading to free.
bank.subs_note_one: Onboarding covered for one performer — one month of ElevenLabs Creator, {sum} in total. A one-off cost, not running: the split survives the performer downgrading to free.
bank.payout_hint: What you owe the rights holders now, and recording what has been paid.
bank.f_row_hint: One row = one management agreement — voice, face or both.
bank.f_face_hint_a: The character must be trained in this bank (
bank.f_fee_hint: What the performer was paid for the recording — for bookkeeping only.
bank.f_tiers_hint: Applies to the customer price at the monthly settlement — for example 10 % off from the 20th use in the same month.
bank.f_exclusive: Exclusive to our bank (our customer network only — can be changed later per performer or in bulk)
bank.err_voice_id: An ElevenLabs voice id is required when the row has a voice.
bank.toggle_off_title: Click to deactivate — the voice disappears from customer menus
bank.apps_off: Off — the “Join the bank as a voice” page says you are not taking applications right now.
bank.events_none: No production has used a performer voice yet.

actorAdmin.waiting_share: ⏳ Waiting for the performer to share their clone — paste the voice id into the rate card below
actorAdmin.excl_note_face: Only your own customer network can use the face.
actorAdmin.excl_note_both: Only your own customer network can use the assets.
actorAdmin.excl_note_voice: Only your own customer network can use the voice.
actorAdmin.excl_note_shared: Every customer on the platform can use the voice — the royalty still goes to you.
actorAdmin.settle_note: The ledger says what has been earned. Here you record what has actually been paid — otherwise “owed” shows the same amount again next month.
actorAdmin.settle_sees_a: The performer sees the same thing at
actorAdmin.settle_no_email: Add an email under “Rates” so the performer can see their own ledger.
actorAdmin.po_err_fields: Fill in the period (two dates) and an amount.
actorAdmin.lic_note: The usage right — medium, territory and term for campaigns; work title and role scope for film and series. The rates above cover generation; the licence is the fee.
actorAdmin.pub_note_a: The card is public and appears in the
actorAdmin.pub_note_off: Publish to get a shareable page with images, samples and bio — and a place in the public gallery.
actorAdmin.demo_note_on: Marked “Example” in the gallery and on the card, shown only on our own domains (TwinLedger + the root), and links to recruitment rather than purchase. Turn it off when a real person takes the place.
actorAdmin.demo_note_off: The card is presented as a person customers can use in production.
actorAdmin.bio_ph: A little about the performer — experience, style, what the voice suits …
actorAdmin.photos_hint: The first image is used as the main image. Flux LoRA images work fine.
actorAdmin.samples_hint: MP3/WAV — for example spot demos in different styles.
actorAdmin.rates_per_kind_hint: Leave the fields empty where the standard rate should apply.
actorAdmin.f_email_hint: Used for approval notices when a customer requires pre-approval.
actorAdmin.f_voice_id_hint: The clone lives on the performer’s own ElevenLabs account and is shared with us. Paste the voice id here once the sharing is done — the voice cannot be used until it is here. An empty field disconnects the voice.
actorAdmin.f_face_hint: Paste the character id from the character training if the performer has also licensed their face (Flux LoRA). Productions using the character are then logged at the “Face” rate above — or the standard rates if it is empty.
actorAdmin.subs_label: We covered the onboarding month at ElevenLabs
actorAdmin.subs_hint: The clone lives on the performer’s own account, which must be on Creator (~220 kr) at the moment it is shared with us. Afterwards the account can be downgraded to free — the sharing survives (confirmed by ElevenLabs 03.09.2026). Tick this if we covered that one month. A one-off cost, not running.
actorAdmin.rates_forward: New rates apply from the next use — the history keeps the rates that applied then.
actorAdmin.err_std_numbers: The standard rates must be numbers.
actorAdmin.err_kind_pair: Fill in both the rate and the price for {kind} — or leave both empty for the standard.
actorAdmin.appr_note: “Free” = the customer may use the voice/face without pre-approval. “Needs approval” = the performer is notified by email and must approve each use — if they do not reply within the deadline, the use is approved automatically.
actorAdmin.appr_none: No customers in the network yet.
actorAdmin.lib_note_on: The voice is shared in ElevenLabs’ global library — and therefore also open to drop-in customers on the platform, without approval per use (cf. the performer agreement). ElevenLabs pays the library income directly to the performer — we are not a party to it.
actorAdmin.lib_note_off: The performer may choose to share the voice in ElevenLabs’ global library — extra income from users worldwide.
actorAdmin.lib_warning: Remember: the voice lives on the performer’s OWN ElevenLabs account and is shared with us — it is the performer who turns library sharing on and off there. This switch only governs the agreement record on our side.
actorAdmin.lib_payout_note: Library income is paid by ElevenLabs straight to the performer’s own Stripe account. It does not pass through us, and we take no share of it. The fields below are only a note to ourselves about what the performer has earned off the platform.
actorAdmin.earn_err_fields: Fill in the period (YYYY-MM) and an amount greater than 0.
actorAdmin.bykind_h2: What the voice has been used for

licences.intro: The usage right, alongside the usage meter. The rate card suggests the price — it can be overridden freely before the agreement is made, and the agreed amount is frozen on the row.
licences.kind_campaign_hint: Time limited and renewable — advertising and marketing.
licences.kind_work_hint: One-off sum, perpetual, bound to the work — film, series, games, audiobooks.
licences.f_work_title_ph: The title of the film or series
licences.warn_channel: Royalty is not possible with other distribution: we then cannot see the income the share is calculated from. Choose TrickleTracks or IndigoBoom, or go for a fixed fee.
licences.note_lag: ⚠️ Streaming income is reported 2–3 months in arrears. The first statement therefore comes a quarter after the release — say so to the rights holder now, not when they ask.
licences.deviation: {sign}{pct} % against list price. The deviation is stored, so the card can be adjusted to reality.
licences.need_title: The work title is missing — the perpetuity is bound to the work, so it cannot be empty.
licences.pv_negative: The customer price does not cover what has been promised away.
licences.stmt_hint: The basis is what we actually received, not the gross from the services.
licences.edit_note: The split is recalculated for every party.
licences.comp_fee_hint: The whole fee now. No share of what the release earns.
licences.comp_hybrid_hint: A reduced fee now, plus a share. The default choice for most.
licences.comp_royalty_hint: Nothing now, all in a share. Greatest upside, longest road to the first krone.

payouts.intro: What {tenant} owes the rights holders right now — earned minus already paid, summed from the ledger. Pay from your bank, then record them as paid here. The money does not pass through the system.
payouts.err_fetch: Could not fetch the payout list
payouts.none_due_empty: The bank has no rights holders yet.
payouts.none_due_paid: Everything earned has been recorded as paid.
payouts.threshold_hint: Amounts below the threshold are held and added next time. Nothing is lost — “owed” is always everything earned minus everything paid.
payouts.step_1: Download the list and pay the amounts from your bank.
payouts.step_2: Come back here and record them as paid. “Paid out” and “Owed” then move in each person’s own ledger.
payouts.note_ph: For example “Monthly settlement September, paid from DNB 3 Oct”
payouts.none_ticked: Nobody is ticked. Lower the threshold or tick rows in the list.
payouts.confirm_one:
Record one payout of {sum} as PAID?

Do this only once the money has actually left your bank. The record appears immediately in the rights holder’s own ledger.
payouts.confirm_many:
Record {n} payouts totalling {sum} as PAID?

Do this only once the money has actually left your bank. The record appears immediately in the rights holder’s own ledger.

casting.no_hits_body: Nobody in the bank fits this. Remove a filter, or loosen the requirements — a wider range takes in more.
casting.truncated: Showing the first {n} of {total}. Narrow it down with the filters.
casting.admin_intro: What a director filters on. Left empty, the rights holder falls out of every filter that uses them — they become invisible, not broadly available.
casting.admin_age_hint: PLAYING AGE, not age: what age they can play. The filter matches OVERLAP, so a wide range gives more hits.
casting.admin_consent_label: The rights holder has expressly consented to a casting range
casting.admin_consent_hint: Casting range is a special category of data (GDPR art. 9) and must be SELF-DECLARED by the rights holder, not set by you. Without consent the field is not stored, and if consent is withdrawn the values are deleted.
casting.max_reached: Maximum {n} in one round. Deselect someone to swap.
